Fix design: in Viewer.tsx onInit, change only the existing controller.stopMove wrapper. When the existing `hovering` flag is true (stopMove is being called from inside showCorner, i.e. the mouse left a hover preview) and the fold position from controller.getCalculation()?.getPosition() has x <= 0, call the existing dropFold(flip) instead of page-flip's stopMove. In every other case keep today's behaviour exactly (position present -> original stopMove, no position -> dropFold). Sketch: const pos = controller.getCalculation()?.getPosition(); return pos && !(hovering && pos.x <= 0) ? stopMove() : dropFold(flip). Add one short comment saying why (a hover preview must never turn the page; on a page narrower than page-flip's fixed 50px fold it rests across the spine, #15).
Make sure `hovering` is declared before the stopMove wrapper uses it (it is declared in the same onInit scope today) and that the wrapper reads it at call time.
After the fix re-run the same reproduction (expect #/p/45) and check every acceptance criterion in the browser; write each viewport and observed result in the report.

Out of scope: patching node_modules or page-flip versions, hiding the preview on small pages, refactoring the other page-flip patches (isPointOnCorners, flipNext/flipPrev, settle, dropFold), the 'mouse leaves the window straight from the corner' case, new files, new dependencies, test tooling, CSS changes.
